Position: Oracle Cloud Technical Architect
The world of payment processing is rapidly evolving, and businesses are looking for loyal and strategic partners to help them grow.
Meet Nuvei . Nuvei is the global fintech building the infrastructure for every payment, everywhere. Its modular, flexible, and scalable technology enables leading companies to accept next-generation payments, offer all payout options, and benefit from card issuing, banking, risk, and fraud management services. Connecting businesses to their customers in more than 200 markets, with local acquiring in 52 markets, 150 currencies, and over 720 alternative payment methods, Nuvei provides the technology and insights for customers and partners to succeed locally and globally through one integration.
At Nuvei , we live our core values, and we thrive on solving complex problems. We are dedicated to continually improving our product and providing relentless customer service. We are always looking for exceptional talent to join us on the journey!
Your Mission
Nuvei is looking for an Oracle Cloud Technical Architect to lead the Oracle technical layer of the UFS Reimagined program within the Global Finance organization. The program is delivering Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP and EPM across the Nuvei finance landscape in two waves, alongside a systems integrator and a number of specialist partners for 3rd party solutions being implemented in parallel. This role will suit someone with ten or more years of Oracle technical experience, including several full Fusion Cloud implementation lifecycles from requirements through cutover and hypercare, who has carried architecture accountability through a security and compliance approval process and has taken a newly implemented ecosystem into a sustained support model.

title: RevOps Contractor
description:
Clozd is the leader in Decision Intelligence, helping companies uncover the truth by capturing direct feedback throughout the customer journey.
We believe most revenue organizations are operating without the full picture. CRM and call data only tell part of the story. Clozd delivers the missing truth layer, giving executives the insights they need to improve win rates, retention, and growth.
We need team members who can tackle ambiguity, solve complex problems, and delight customers. We hire dynamic employees who take initiative, find ways to simplify and scale, possess strong interpersonal and communication skills, value humility and learning, crave a fast-paced startup environment, and never compromise their integrity.
As a RevOps Contractor, you'll own the systems Clozd 's go-to-market team runs on. This is a part-time (~20 hours/week), hands-on engagement for an experienced Salesforce admin who loves clean data and well-scoped projects. You'll administer Salesforce, keep our data clean and trustworthy across Salesforce and Gong, and ship a set of high-priority systems projects. You'll work closely with our GTM Strategy and Ops and Data & AI teams.
What you will be doing:
●Own day-to-day Salesforce administration for our 50+ person sales, CS, and
marketing teams, triaging and resolving requests from reps, managers, and leadership
around permission sets, page layouts, flows, and user support
● Lead a Salesforce hygiene audit and cleanup, including duplicate rules, validation
rules, field rationalization, and stage and record-type definitions
● Execute territory and book reassignments as we restructure our AE and AM books,
including the bulk ownership changes and the reporting to track them
● Build the Salesforce objects, fields, and dashboards for renewal ownership and
retention tracking, retiring the spreadsheets that hold this today
● Audit and tune our Gong, Salesforce, and BigQuery integrations, document what
syncs where, fix what's broken, and troubleshoot integration breaks within one

business day

● Create a data dictionary for the Salesforce fields and objects our BigQuery reporting
depends on, so our analytics don't rely on tribal knowledge
● Build declarative flows (and light scripting where needed) that remove manual work
from the revenue team
● Leave everything better documented than you found it, with a clear map of our
systems, integrations, and known data issues, plus a written handoff for anything that
needs ongoing care

Qualifications:

● 3+ years of experience administering Salesforce, ideally at more than one company
(Salesforce certification a plus, not required)
● Deep comfort with data hygiene, reporting structure, and CRM governance, including
experience cleaning up someone else's org
● Hands-on experience with Gong and at least one of Outreach, HubSpot, or a similar
sales engagement tool, including their Salesforce sync
● Some scripting or automation experience (light Python, Zapier, n8n, or similar) and
comfort going beyond point-and-click configuration
● Familiarity with BigQuery or another data warehouse fed by Salesforce is a plus

● Strong ownership and independence, with the ability to drive a scope to completion,
flag early when something is bigger than it looked, and document what you built so it

lasts

● Availability for a consistent ~20 hours a week during US Mountain business hours,
with the ability to respond to break/fix issues within one business day
● Alignment with Clozd 's core values: vision, drive, empathy, stewardship, authenticity,

and integrity

Engagement Details
● Type: Independent contractor (1099 or through your own entity)
● Hours: ~20 hours/week, billed hourly against a monthly cap
● Term: 3-month initial term, then month-to-month with 2 weeks' notice either way
● Location: Remote, US-based; Mountain time overlap preferred
● Start: As soon as possible

Clozd is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Clozd does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender

title: Data Engineer - Senior JP992
description:
Project Name:
Digital Regulatory Assurance System
Scope:
Modernization initiatives across the Government of Alberta are fundamentally changing how ministry users collect, manage, analyze, and use data as legacy systems are transformed into modern Data Management and Geospatial Platforms. This requires seamless data integration across multiple legacy and modern platforms to create a trusted, unified source of information.
DRAS is a Government of Alberta regulatory transformation initiative led by Environment and Protected Areas (EPA) to modernize, digitize, and streamline environmental and natural resource regulatory processes. DRAS supports the full regulatory lifecycle, from application and authorization to monitoring, compliance, remediation, and closure through a single, consolidated digital platform
As DRAS development continues, the volume, variety, and complexity of structured data continue to grow, creating a sustained need for dedicated data engineering and data integration expertise. The Talend Integration Analyst designs, builds, operates, and supports data integration solutions on the Government of Alberta's Talend Integration Platform, to move, transform, and consolidate data across ministry systems, cloud services, and analytics environments, and operational systems.
This is a hands-on technical role for someone who combines strong Talend and SQL development skills with a disciplined, service-oriented approach to platform operations including job scheduling, monitoring, error handling, and incident resolution; while collaborating with data engineers, platform administrators, ministry stakeholders, and vendor support partners.
This position will primarily support the Digital Regulatory Assurance System (DRAS) program, the role may be expanded to support additional enterprise data initiatives.
Duties :

• Demonstrated hands-on experience developing data integration solutions with Talend (Data Integration / Data Fabric / Talend Studio)

• Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational databases (e.g., Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL).

• Proven experience designing ETL/ELT processes, data mappings, and transformation logic for enterprise data.

• Experience operating and supporting integration jobs in a production environment, including scheduling, monitoring, and incident resolution.

• Translate business and data requirements into robust technical designs, applying data-mapping, transformation, and reconciliation logic

• Build parameterized, reusable, and context-aware jobs that promote cleanly across development, test, and production environments.

• Implement performance-tuned, scalable integration patterns for both batch and near-real-time data movement.

• Design and expose secure data services and APIs using Azure API Management for downstream systems.

• Implement data governance practices, including metadata management, data classification, and lineage tracking.

• Ensure compliance with privacy and regulatory standards (e.g., POPA) through role-based access controls, encryption, and data masking.

• Design, develop, and unit-test Talend integration jobs, routes, and reusable components to extract, transform, and load data between source systems, databases, files, APIs, and cloud storage

• Schedule, orchestrate, deploy, and monitor Talend jobs; proactively track execution, throughput, and failures.

• Provide day-to-day operational support including triage, troubleshooting, and resolve integration incidents and data-load failures within agreed service levels.

• Monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines and integrations, ensuring reliability, scalability, and performance across the platform.

• Utilize AI and automation tools to streamline data engineering workflows, including pipeline development, testing, monitoring, and documentation.

• Leverage AI-assisted tools for code generation, optimization, and review to improve development efficiency and code quality.

• Other duties as needed

title: Download Support Analyst
description:
About Keystone

Keystone is one of the largest and fastest-growing insurance brokerages in the country - ranked #26 among U.S. retail brokers and #4 fastest-growing in the Top 50 by Business Insurance. Our platform spans 33+ states, 180+ agency partners, and more than $500 million in revenue - uniting some of the country's most respected independent agencies with the scale, tools, and resources of a national brokerage. Through operational support in finance, HR, marketing, technology, producer development, and M&A, we empower agencies to grow while preserving what makes them who they are - their client relationships and their role in the communities they serve. Guided by our trademarked commitment, "Trust, our most important policy," Keystone is building the insurance solution every family and business can count on. For more information, visit .

Download Support Analyst

Position Summary:

The Download Support Analyst is an operational support position reporting to the Enterprise Download Manager. It focuses on ensuring reliable day-to-day carrier download operations by monitoring download activity, resolving suspense and exception items, troubleshooting carrier connectivity issues, coordinating with carriers and IVANS, and supporting agency management system conversions. The role also serves as a support point for business teams, helps maintain documentation, and tracks recurring issues to improve download processes, automation, and enterprise standardization.

Key Responsibilities:

• Monitor daily carrier download activity and identify failed, missing, delayed, or incomplete download transactions.

• Process suspense queues and resolve download exceptions in accordance with enterprise procedures and service level expectations.

• Research and troubleshoot carrier download issues, escalating complex connectivity or system issues to the Enterprise Download Manager, carriers, IVANS, or technology partners as needed.

• Support download testing, validation, cutover, and post-conversion stabilization activities for agency management system conversions and acquired books of business.

• Maintain accurate documentation of download issues, resolutions, carrier setup requirements, and process updates.

• Assist business teams with questions related to carrier download workflow, suspense handling, and download best practices.

• Track recurring issues and exception trends to support process improvement, automation opportunities, and enterprise download standardization.

Qualifications:

• Minimum of 4 years of insurance operations experience with expertise in carrier download and agency management systems.

• Hands-on experience with Applied Epic and Microsoft Office Suite required.

• Deep knowledge of IVANS connectivity and policy, claims, commissions, and eDocs download processes.

• Proven ability to manage cross-functional projects and collaborate with carriers, technology teams, and business stakeholders.

ABOUT FACTORY

Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the PM for Growth at Factory, you’ll own our overall approach to get users active and productive on the platform.

You’ll be responsible for our activation metric: how do we measure what it means to be an activated user, and how do we get more users to that point and beyond, whether they’re coming from our self-serve product or onboarding via an enterprise deployment.

And you’ll own our self-serve product offering: what we provide as part of it, how we price and package it, the role it plays in our broader company strategy, and how we should evaluate its success.

There won’t be a single “growth” engineering team to work with-you’ll operate across multiple engineering pods and work closely with our Marketing, BizOps, and Deployment functions to make sure we’re doing the right things to create more happy Factory users.

You’ll need a strong thesis for what makes a compelling early software factory experience in a competitive market, and an opinion about how PLG best reinforces a top-down Enterprise motion. You’ll need sharp technical instincts, genuine empathy for developers, and the ability to make fast, high-quality decisions in ambiguity. You should be as comfortable diving into technical architecture discussions as you are presenting roadmap priorities to leadership.

Our goal with the product function at Factory is to be high-leverage, high-ownership, and hands-on-you can expect to be working directly with the C-suite at the largest companies in the world, and shipping improvements directly to the product. And you’ll be central to defining the role of Product in a software factory-driven organization-a pattern we intend to pioneer and then help distribute across our customer base and the broader industry.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

- Own the roadmap for multiple major areas of our product

- Partner closely with customers and work closely with data to understand pain points and translate them into product improvements.

- Work with engineering and research to ship features that keep Factory at the frontier of AI-powered development.

- Build frameworks and processes that scale as the product team grows.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years of experience spanning product and engineering roles, including a deep developer tools background or at least one year in an engineering role

- Experience leading Growth teams in an Enterprise context, bringing a fast-paced and scientific mindset to product development.

- Strong technical foundation, with experience partnering closely with engineering teams to design, build, and ship complex technical products.

- Proven ability to drive product launches, from concept through release, with evidence of meaningful user adoption or commercial impact.

- Actively engaged with the AI ecosystem, staying current on coding agents, model capabilities, and emerging industry trends through hands-on experimentation.Thrive in fast-moving, high-ambiguity environments and take ownership end-to-end.

The team works in the office 5 days a week in San Francisco (walking distance to Caltrain).

Why this role exists
The architecture set in this role decides which certifications One Identity can hold and which markets we can sell into. That is unusual commercial weight for an engineering seat, and it comes with a mandate from leadership to build the program behind it.
We sell on-premises and hosted solutions. Some products run as hosted services we operate in Azure and AWS. Others ship as software customers deploy in their own datacenters. Infrastructure security here has two audiences: the environments we run, and the base images, container definitions, and deployment defaults we publish, which become part of every customer's environment. A hardening decision made once is inherited by everyone who deploys it.
We're separating from Quest Software and building an independent security function. The team is lean and globally distributed, and this role is its senior technical voice. Scope comes from what you design and automate, and from what engineering chooses to adopt.
What you'll do
Shape the architecture

• Own security architecture across Azure and AWS: tenant, subscription and account design, network segmentation and traffic control, private connectivity, egress policy, workload isolation. Where a regulated market or a certification constrains a design, you're expected to know before it's committed.

• Run our own products against real security requirements and tell us what you find. IT operates our privileged access controls on One Identity software, so you'll see how our products hold up under production pressure and take that back to the teams building them.

• Bring engineering into architectural decisions early. Designs teams help shape are the ones that hold up in production.

Raise the engineering bar

• Teams already build with infrastructure as code across both clouds. Raise the security ceiling inside that practice: hardened modules, secure-by-default landing zones and account baselines, and patterns teams reach for because they're better.

• Extend policy as code across the pipeline and the platform so teams get a signal at commit time.

• Own the hardened image pipeline for virtual machines and containers, covering the fleet we run and the images we publish: build, patch cadence, provenance, signing, and the automation that keeps both current.

• Secure the container orchestration layer, including the reference architecture and secure defaults customers inherit when they deploy our products on their own clusters.

• Set the security architecture for AI workloads: model and inference endpoint exposure, data boundaries and residency, identity for agents and service principals, secrets handling, and guardrails around AI tooling in the development lifecycle.

• Own infrastructure vulnerability and exposure management end to end: discovery, prioritization weighing exploitability and reachability alongside severity, ownership routing, remediation tracking, verification. Where we can act ourselves, it arrives as a pull request against the module, image definition, or policy that produced it. PRs, not tickets.

title: Import Compliance Manager
description:
JOB SUMMARY:
The Import Compliance Manager is responsible for ensuring the company's import operations comply with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations and all applicable trade laws. This role oversees the accurate classification of imported goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), manages relationships with customs brokers and freight forwarders, and coordinates the end-to-end flow of container shipments from origin to destination, including bonded warehouse operations and duty drawback recovery. The ideal candidate combines deep trade compliance expertise with hands-on experience managing container logistics and import documentation.
JOB DUTIES:

• Manage the classification of imported products under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), ensuring accuracy and consistency across the product catalog.

• Oversee end-to-end container import operations, including booking, customs clearance, port coordination, and delivery to distribution centers or warehouses.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customs brokers, freight forwarders, and carriers to resolve clearance delays, documentation discrepancies, and duty disputes.

• Ensure compliance with CBP regulations, Importer Security Filing (ISF) requirements, and other federal import/export regulations.

• Maintain and audit import records, entry summaries, and classification rulings to support recordkeeping requirements and prepare for CBP audits.

• Manage bonded warehouse operations, including inventory control, CBP-mandated recordkeeping, withdrawal entries, and coordination with warehouse operators to ensure compliance with 19 CFR Part 19.

• Monitor changes in tariff schedules, trade agreements, and duty rates (including Section 301, antidumping/countervailing duties) and assess their impact on the business.

• Identify and pursue duty savings opportunities, including free trade agreement eligibility, bonded warehouse deferral strategies, duty drawback, and first sale valuation.

• Administer the company's duty drawback program end-to-end: identify eligible import/export transactions, prepare and file drawback claims, maintain supporting documentation, and manage relationships with drawback service providers or brokers to maximize duty recovery.

• Partner with procurement, finance, and legal teams to evaluate landed cost impacts of tariff changes and sourcing decisions.

• Develop and maintain internal compliance policies, standard operating procedures, and training materials for classification and import processes.

• Manage and mentor import compliance analysts or coordinators, as applicable.

• Track key performance metrics related to container transit times, customs clearance rates, and compliance audit outcomes.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's degree in International Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or related field.

• 5+ years of experience in import compliance, customs brokerage, or international trade, with direct experience in HTS classification. Strong working knowledge of CBP regulations, Incoterms, and international shipping documentation (bills of lading, commercial invoices, certificates of origin).

• Experience managing container shipments and coordinating with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.

• Experience with bonded warehouse (Class 3) operations and duty drawback claim preparation and filing.

• Familiarity with trade compliance software and ERP/TMS systems (e.g., SAP GTS, Oracle GTM, Descartes).

• Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) credential preferred, not required.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and cross-functional communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple shipments and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

$90,000 to $120,000, DOE

title: Staff Engineer

About AlphaSense: 

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

About the Team:

The User Management team owns the full identity lifecycle at AlphaSense - from creating and provisioning users, through managing their identities, to authenticating who they are and authorizing what they can do in the system. Our work spans three core domains:

• User Management - creating, provisioning, and managing user identities

• Authentication - verifying who users are

• Authorization - determining what users can do in the system

We are a product platform team, not a product team: we build the identity and access infrastructure that other engineering teams build on top of, rather than shipping user-facing features ourselves. We also act as a security guardrail for AlphaSense, since identity and access sit at the center of how the platform stays secure.

The team is well-established and senior, based in Helsinki, Finland. We're now expanding into North America - with roles based in both Canada and the US - to build follow-the-sun coverage, so our customers get proper support around the clock, and to push deliberately toward a true platform model - scaling our authentication and authorization systems so they can be safely self-served by teams across the company.

About the Role: 

This is a Staff Engineer role on the team that manages identity and access for AlphaSense's entire, and constantly growing, customer base, and that nearly every product engineering team depends on for user and entitlement data. You'll work across all three pillars of identity: creating and managing users, authenticating them, and authorizing what they can do - designing systems built to scale with a constantly growing number of users. Security is core to this role, not adjacent to it - you'll work closely with our security teams to make sure what we build is secure by design, in an environment governed by SOC2 and GDPR.

We're looking for a genuinely senior, self-sufficient engineer with strong experience building and operating identity, authentication, or authorization platforms at scale, ideally in a platform/product-platform engineering context. This is someone who doesn't just execute a roadmap, but helps understand the needs behind it, shapes it, and then drives execution - largely autonomously, and in close collaboration with our core team based in Helsinki. You're genuinely interested in security, comfortable partnering closely with security teams on secure-by-design systems, and comfortable working in a distributed, cross-timezone setup - based in North America, collaborating closely with a Helsinki-based team.

title: Healthcare Project Manager
description:
ABOUT US
Verian Lithuania (formerly PPMI ) is a European policy research and evaluation consultancy. We work primarily for EU institutions (European Commission, JRC, DG SANTE, HaDEA, EUDA, ECDC) and international organisations (OECD, UN). Our public health and life sciences portfolio is growing fast, and we are looking for an experienced Healthcare Project Manager to help us deliver it.
THE ROLE
We are looking for a project manager to lead large-scale, complex EU-funded healthcare projects: multi-year, often multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams, high-profile EU clients and demanding delivery standards. You will be accountable for delivery from kick-off to final reporting, including budgets, timelines, teams and client relationships.
Our portfolio includes European guidelines for prostate cancer, evidence-based research prioritisation in the drugs field, GRADE evidence assessments, and quality indicator development following Cochrane standards. You will work closely with our review methodologists, so a good understanding of how systematic reviews and guidelines are developed will help you plan, steer and quality-assure this work as we grow our in-house evidence synthesis capacity.
Day-to-day, you would:

• Lead projects end to end: work planning, timelines, budgets, risk management and quality assurance of deliverables

• Manage several projects and workstreams in parallel, setting priorities and allocating resources across teams

• Act as the main point of contact for EU clients, including inception, interim and final reporting in line with contractual requirements

• Lead multidisciplinary teams of researchers, review methodologists, external experts and consortium partners

• Organise and steer working groups, expert panels and stakeholder consultations

• Oversee the planning and quality of systematic reviews, GRADE assessments, guideline development and quality indicator work, in close collaboration with methodologists

• Drive the use of innovative and AI-assisted review tools in project workflows

• Lead or contribute to tenders and proposals for EU evidence synthesis and health contracts

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Essential:

• PhD in public health, epidemiology, health sciences or a related field

• Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex projects (e.g., multi-year, multi-partner contracts with several parallel workstreams), ideally EU-funded healthcare or public health projects such as service or framework contracts with the European Commission and its agencies, EU4Health or Horizon Europe

• Experience holding full responsibility for project budgets, timelines, risk management and contractual reporting

• Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing senior client and stakeholder relationships

• Excellent written and spoken English

Strong assets:

• Understanding of how systematic reviews and clinical guidelines are developed (e.g., Cochrane methodology, PRISMA, GRADE, Evidence-to-Decision frameworks)

• Hands-on systematic review experience as an author or review team member

• Experience in cancer evidence review, such as screening, diagnosis, treatment guidelines or HTA

• Track record of writing or leading successful EU tender proposals

• Experience with AI/ML tools in evidence synthesis or health data analysis (e.g., AI-assisted screening, text mining, bibliometrics)

• Publications in cancer, screening, HTA or guideline development

• Familiarity with review and analysis tools (e.g., RevMan, GRADEpro, Covidence, R, Python)

• Experience drafting policy or regulatory documents

CONDITIONS

• Monthly service fee: EUR 4,000-4,500, depending on experience

• Full-time equivalent commitment with flexible working hours

• Remote work within the EU

• Service contract with possibility of extension

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your CV and a short cover letter by 6 November 2026, highlighting your experience managing EU-funded healthcare projects and any relevant work in cancer

title: Operations Lead - Process Change
description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the Role

Reports to the Operations Principal, Change. The Strategic Operations team sits between Product, Technology, and Claims Operations and owns the work that turns a new way of working into one the organization actually runs on.

Not every change at Reserv arrives with a product release behind it. Programs change, client requirements change, and the way a claim is handled changes with them. We are hiring an Operations Lead to own process design and change across claims operations, so that how work is done is written down, current, and changed deliberately.

You own the process side of the function: before-and-after process design for each change, the SOP library and how it is governed, verification that changes landed in practice, and the training and communications for process changes. You will work alongside the Operations Lead who owns product change, since most product releases also change a process, and with claims leadership, who own the work you are documenting. You will be an excellent fit if you have redesigned how an operations team works, can write a process someone will follow, and verify that changes landed in practice.

Duties & Responsibilities

Process Design: Lead the before-and-after process design for each change, product-driven or not, working with leaders, managers, and team leads on what actually shifts in their day. Write the end-to-end process so it can be followed without further explanation, and pressure-test it with the people who will run it before it goes live.

SOP Ownership and Governance: Own the SOP library across lines of business and account variants: its structure, its currency, and its governance. Draft the standard language for each change, drive it into every affected SOP through the SOP owners against a date, and build the auditability that shows who changed what and when. Partner with the Principal on the platform and workflow the library should run on.

Change Readiness for Process Changes: Run process changes against the readiness standard: documented process, approved change plan, training and communications plan, onboarding updated, and metrics defined. Assemble the evidence for sign-off and flag gaps early.

Training, Enablement, and Communications: Build and execute the training and communications for process changes for leaders, managers, and frontline teams, and coordinate with Learning & Development so new-hire onboarding teaches the current process.

Verification and Feedback: Go back after each change and verify it landed in practice, through SOP checks, time studies, and conversations with the teams doing the work. Carry what you find back to the Principal and to claims leadership, and feed it into how the next change is designed.

Metric and Data Management: This person will be responsible for continually tracking metrics to determine success and make data-driven changes to rollouts

title: Langfuse - Senior Backend Engineer (US-East)
description:
WHY BACKEND ENGINEERING AT LANGFUSE

Your work will have an outsized impact.

Langfuse ingests terabytes of AI tracing data per day. When a Fortune 50 company instruments their application with Langfuse, they hit the infrastructure you built. Everything you ship is open source and immediately visible.

The core of your role is making Langfuse fast and affordable at scale: owning the ingestion pipeline, optimizing ClickHouse data models and queries so dashboards load instantly, and building the backend abstractions that let product engineers ship data-heavy features without reinventing the plumbing each time.

You will also make sure Langfuse runs everywhere. You’ll operate Langfuse Cloud across multiple production environments, and make self-hosting effortless. You will support a single Docker Compose setup to enterprise-grade Helm chart deployment.

 

You won’t be solving these problems alone. Langfuse is now part of ClickHouse, which means the people who built the database you’re optimizing are one channel away. Few backend roles give you that kind of access to the internals of your core datastore.

 

YOU WILL GROW AT LANGFUSE BY

- Own and optimize our ingestion pipeline: Langfuse ingests massive volumes of tracing data through a pipeline that flows from our API to ClickHouse. You'll work on throughput, latency, reliability, and cost efficiency at every stage of this pipeline.

- Make ClickHouse fast: our tracing data lives in ClickHouse. You'll design schemas, optimize merge strategies, tune batch inserts, write and review analytical queries that power dashboards and the UI. You'll become an expert on ClickHouse internals - and you'll have the ClickHouse database engineering team one channel away.

- Build new infrastructure-heavy features: things like LLM-as-a-Judge (where we post-process large volumes of ingested data asynchronously), alerting at scale, client-code execution, or batch dataset operations. Build the foundation and, if you like, dip your toes into the frontend for those.

- Test with real data in production: when evaluating a new ClickHouse schema, migration, or query optimization, you'll run load tests against production data to validate that changes actually improve things. We don't guess at performance. We prototype new table designs, run them in parallel on real traffic, and compare before committing.

- Scale for what's next: we're growing fast and new product directions like complex long-running agent observability and real-time evaluation push the infrastructure in new ways. You'll be thinking ahead about what breaks at 10x scale.

 

LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR INFRASTRUCTURE

- From Zero to Scale: Langfuse's Infrastructure Evolution https://langfuse.com/blog/2024-12-langfuse-v3-infrastructure-evolution - deep dive into how we went from Postgres to ClickHouse

- Max talking infrastructure at ClickHouse OpenHouse Amsterdam https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NXYQ5odATrM - recording of our CTO walking through the architecture

- Architecture https://langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Strong backend engineer who gets excited about database internals, query optimization, and distributed systems

- You get excited when working with a ton of data

- Experience with analytical databases, data pipelines, or high-throughput event processing. ClickHouse experience is a big plus but not required

- You organize yourself. You have strong opinions about what to build and how to ship it

- Comfortable reading and writing TypeScript (our backend) and SQL

- Thrives in a small, accountable team where your output is visible and matters

- CS or quantitative degree preferred

 

Bonus points:

- Former founder

- Background in building data-intensive systems at scale

Dafür läuft bei uns ein eingespielter Prozess: Wir wissen, welche Werbeanzeigen funktionieren, wie die Texte aufgebaut sind und wie eine Kampagne aussehen muss und welche Handgriffe es in Meta für eine erfolgreiche Kampagne braucht.
Genau diesen Prozess sollst du bei uns abarbeiten - Schritt für Schritt, Kampagne für Kampagne.
Wir wachsen weiter und suchen deshalb Unterstützung bei der Durchführung unserer Projekte.
Deine Aufgaben
Grundvoraussetzung für diese Stelle: Anlegen von Kampagnen in Meta (Verwendung des Ad Managers von Meta)
Eingabe und Änderung von Meta/Facebook/Instagram Werbeanzeigen (Ads) im Meta Business Manager
Du legst unsere Kunden in BVS an und erstellst die Verknüpfungen, so dass die Bewerber auch an den Kunden weitergeleitet werden.
Betreuen unserer Recruiting-Kampagnen in enger Zusammenarbeit mit unserer Projektleiterin, nach unserem bestehenden System
Als Urlaubsvertretung übernimmst du die Gestaltung von Kampagnen in Canva und erstellst die passenden Texte für neue Kampagnen. Du arbeitest mit unseren Vorlagen und setzt daraus ansprechende Anzeigen und Grafiken um.
Du musst nicht (!) zwingend Vorerfahrung im Recruiting, HR oder Projektmanagement haben
Das bringst du mit
Du hast eingehende Erfahrung im Umgang mit Meta (Facebook/Instagram). Du hast Freude daran Anzeigen anzulegen, zu ändern und zu kontrollieren.
Das Wichtigste vorweg: Unser Prozess steht, er funktioniert, und er ist in Vorlagen und Abläufen festgehalten. Deine Aufgabe ist es, ihn sauber, genau und verlässlich abzuarbeiten - nicht, ihn neu zu erfinden.
Sorgfalt und Genauigkeit sind uns wichtiger als originelle Einfälle. Wer gerne nach einem klaren System arbeitet, ist bei uns richtig.
Du hast ein gutes Gespür dafür, wann etwas ansprechend aussieht? Dann freuen wir uns auf dich.
Offenheit und Interesse an neuen Ideen, Programmen und Tools
Eigenständiges Denken und sauberes, strukturiertes Arbeiten mit Hausverstand sind für dich selbstverständlich und keine Ausnahme.
Du kannst gut damit umgehen, dass kurzfristige Todos immer wieder aufploppen, und priorisierst Aufgaben.
Du arbeitest nicht nach starren Zeiten - kannst dich gut organisieren und einteilen.
Sehr guter Umgang mit dem Computer (Windows oder Mac, MS Office)
Regelmäßige Kommunikation deiner Fortschritte in internen Online-Meetings
Ein Hinweis in eigener Sache: Ausgebildete und erfahrene Grafikerinnen und Grafiker sind bei uns unterfordert - die Aufgabe ist die Umsetzung mit Vorlagen, nicht die freie Gestaltung.
Das bieten wir
Teilzeit (25-30 Stunden / Woche), auf Wunsch später mehr
Gemeinsame Zusammenarbeit online im kleinen Team mit eigener Verantwortung
Du kannst nach unserem eigens entwickelten System arbeiten und bekommst alles beigebracht
100% Arbeit aus dem Home-Office möglich - bitte keine Digitalen Nomaden

title: Web Scraping Specialist
description:
Position Overview:
We are seeking a highly skilled Web Scraping Architect to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining web scraping processes to gather data from various online sources efficiently and accurately. • Data Cleansing and Validation: Cleanse and validate the collected data to eliminate errors, inconsistencies, and duplicates. Ensure data integrity and accuracy throughout the process.

• Compliance and Legal Considerations: Stay up-to-date with legal and ethical considerations related to web scraping, including website terms of service, copyright, and privacy regulations.

• Documentation: Maintain detailed documentation of web scraping processes, data sources, and methodologies. Create clear and concise instructions for others to follow.

• Collaboration: Collaborate with other teams such as data analysts, developers, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements and deliver insights effectively.

• Security: Implement security measures to ensure the confidentiality and protection of sensitive data throughout the scraping process.

• Proven experience of 4+ years as a Web Scraping Specialist or similar role, with a track record of successful web scraping projects.

• Knowledge on browser fingerprinting

• Has leadership experience.

• Proficiency in programming languages commonly used for web scraping, such as Python, BeautifulSoup, Scrapy, or Selenium.

• Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS, XPath, and other web technologies relevant to web scraping and Coding.

• Knowledge and experience in best of class data storage and retrieval of large volume of scraped data.

• Understanding of web scraping best practices, including handling dynamic content, user-agent rotation, and IP address management.

• Attention to detail and the ability to handle and process large volumes of data accurately.

• Familiarity with data cleansing techniques and data validation processes.

• Good communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Knowledge of web scraping ethics, legal considerations, and compliance with website terms of service.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing web environments

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, or related fields.

• Experience with cloud-based solutions and distributed web scraping systems.

• Knowledge of machine learning techniques for data extraction and natural language

Citizens Against Government Waste (CAGW) offers a wide variety of opportunities to college students across the country. Unpaid research, communications, and government affairs internships are available on a year-round basis and can vary in length from a semester to a few weeks in duration. Interns can choose to work part-time or full-time, as hours of work are extremely flexible. Our daily work with Capitol Hill and the White House, as well as government agencies and other nonprofit organizations, provides a close and invaluable look at how Washington works. Since CAGW maintains a small staff, interns gain hands-on experience in all aspects of CAGW’s activities. Many projects involve working closely with staff members, while others require a great deal of independence. Interns are considered important members of our staff and actively participate in staff meetings and other events. While interns will also be required to perform clerical duties from time to time, much of the work will be substantive.
Research Internship
Assist in formulating policy papers and collect data for original investigative studies. Research and write for CAGW’s annual publications, which include the Congressional Pig Book, Prime Cuts, Government WasteWatch eNews, and special projects, including issue briefs, and policy papers. Interns will have the opportunity to initiate projects. Research internships are also available in specific areas, including healthcare and science, technology and telecommunications, federal regulations and taxation.

Stand Together Fellowships believes that diversity in experiences, perspectives, knowledge and ideas fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. Our admissions office treats all program participants and applicants with honesty, dignity, respect and sensitivity. We welcome all qualified applicants regardless of color, race, religion, religious creed, sex, gender or gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, ethnicity, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy (including medical needs which may arise from pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), military and veteran status, genetic information, marital or familial status, political affiliation, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances.

title: GM - Relief to Hire
description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

Roo Veterinary is building the modern labor marketplace and operating system for veterinary care. We help hospitals reliably staff shifts and access great veterinary professionals, so care happens when it's needed, without burning out teams.

We're hiring a General Manager to run Relief-to-Hire, the business that turns relief work on Roo into full-time hires. Hospitals book relief veterinarians and technicians on Roo every day, and some of those shifts turn into job offers. Relief-to-Hire makes that a product: hospitals try before they hire and pay a placement fee only when a hire happens. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the management team, you'll own the Relief-to-Hire P&L (placement revenue, contribution margin, and the investment decisions behind them) and be accountable for making Roo the way veterinary practices hire, instead of a job ad or a recruiter.

Relief-to-Hire is an established, growing business: hundreds of hospitals have hired through it, and it has grown every year alongside the relief marketplace it's built on. Until now it has been run by a cross-functional squad rather than a dedicated owner; in January 2027 it becomes its own business unit with a P&L, a budget and a GM. You'll lead a small placement team directly, set priorities for a dedicated product manager and growth analyst, and get much of your leverage from design, engineering, lifecycle marketing and data partners you don't manage. The core of the job: generate hiring intent, use product and automation to turn one-sided interest into mutual interest, and focus people on closing hires.

Key Responsibilities

• Own Relief-to-Hire revenue and contribution margin against plan, and set a plan that beats the business's momentum when the evidence supports it.

• Write the business strategy and the scorecard behind it: the funnel from relief relationships to hand-raises, mutual interest, closed placements and average fee, with one owner per metric.

• Allocate budget and headcount by ROI: invest in product and automation before people, and put people where a human closes the hire.

• Design pricing and terms as one system (placement fee, guarantee, payment plans, enterprise caps and lookbacks) and manage the cash cycle from agreement through invoice and collection.

• Define and own the Relief-to-Hire category with Marketing, so "try before you hire" becomes the default way a practice hires and the term points to Roo.

• Set product priorities for the hiring flow, the recruiter tool and lifecycle campaigns with your product manager and designer; build what only Relief-to-Hire needs and partner with the platform team on shared infrastructure.

• Partner with the Enterprise, Independent Hospitals, Veterinary and Technician GMs on shared supply: agree how placements are credited and what they cost, and make Relief-to-Hire easy for their teams to sell.

• Build and lead the placement team: hire to a high bar, measure and pay on closed hires and cash collected, act on underperformance early, and develop the people who hold hospital relationships.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will:

• Grow placement revenue above plan, with contribution margin inside the guardrail agreed with Finance.

• Grow Relief-to-Hire faster than the relief marke

About the Role:
One owner for the entire risk function at a fintech operating between crypto and traditional payments. You will own enterprise risk end to end, including the risk framework and appetite, DORA and operational resilience, B2B partner risk, fraud risk appetite, capital adequacy, and risk gating for new products.
It is an individual contributor role reporting directly to the CEO, with a seat on the leadership team. You will work daily with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Technology, and the B2B Partnerships team. The foundations are in place (risk register, appetite framework, DORA workstreams). The function needs an owner who proactively surfaces risk, takes a position, and stands behind it.
What You'll Do:
Enterprise Risk & Governance:

• Own the enterprise risk framework: risk register, risk appetite statement, taxonomy, and escalation policy.

• Run the risk reporting cycle: structured updates to the CEO and leadership, plus regulatory risk reporting.

• Chair or co-chair the risk committee: agenda, cadence, participants, and decision authority.

• Build risk ownership across business units.

DORA & Operational Resilience:

• Own the DORA ICT risk framework and lead the Register of Information workstream ahead of the 2027 submission window.

• Own business continuity and disaster recovery planning.

• Own third-party and vendor risk: critical providers, concentration risk, and exit planning.

• Own the PSD2 operational resilience framework, including 4-hour major incident reporting and impact tolerances.

• Partner with the CTO and Head of Security on technology and cloud risk.

EMI & Regulatory Risk:

• Lead the operational risk framework and capital adequacy/safeguarding design for two parallel EMI applications (EU and UK).

• Own ongoing capital adequacy monitoring and escalate breaches.

• Own preparation for risk-focused regulatory examinations and act as the primary contact for risk-related regulator queries.

• Coordinate with Legal on regulatory obligations and with the Chief of Compliance on AML/CTF risk appetite.

B2B Partner & Counterparty Risk:

• Design and own the partner risk assessment framework: onboarding scoring, ongoing due diligence, and risk-tiered monitoring.

• Own risk sign-off on material partnerships, define thresholds for CEO approval, and keep high-risk reviews fast and credible.

• Define which industries, geographies, and business models the company will and will not serve.

• Manage partner concentration risk and delegated-compliance liability as B2B volume scales.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk:

• Build a unified fraud risk framework and appetite across relevant functions, with clear ownership and a single escalation path.

• Set fraud risk appetite by channel, product, and geography, and own decisions when thresholds are breached.

• Coordinate with the Chief of Compliance on the fraud/AML overlap.

• Own the sanctions screening risk framework and escalation policy.

Product & Financial Risk:

• Own product-launch risk gating for new products, markets, and business lines.

• Own counterparty credit risk: liquidity providers, banking partners, card schemes, and B2B clients.

• Oversee treasury risk: balances, currency exposure, and concentration.

• Hands-on experience with at least one of: DORA ICT risk framework, MiCA capital adequacy and risk requirements, PSD2 operational resilience, or FCA operational resilience.

title: Data Science Tech Lead Manager, Model Experience
locationText: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company's mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world.

You'll be the senior data science leader for Model Experience and a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders. Working where frontier AI research reaches the public, you'll help shape model roadmap and launch decisions, bringing a point of view on how users experience our models and what good looks like beyond benchmark scores. As a tech lead manager, you'll also hire and manage a team of data scientists, setting their agenda, personally leading the highest-stakes analyses, and raising the bar for how data shapes model and product decisions.

Responsibilities:

• Act as a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders, helping shape model roadmap priorities, launch decisions, and the major bets the team makes

• Set the data science agenda for Model Experience, deciding where the team can have the most impact on model development and launch decisions and what it should deprioritize

• Hire, manage, and develop a team of data scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions

• Frame the most important and ambiguous questions about model quality and user experience, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction

• Define how Model Experience measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks across external products and internal testing that align teams and leadership on what matters

• Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Model Experience, including where launches lack a clean A/B test, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses

• Turn complex analyses of model and user behavior into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners

• Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Model Experience needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our models and products evolve

You may be a good fit if you:

• Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a product or research area at significant scale

• Have 3+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction, hiring, and developing senior data scientists

• Have been a trusted partner to senior product, research, and business leaders, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision

• Bring strong product sense and business judgment, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information

• Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others' technical work

• Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences

• Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress

• Care about the company's mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we opened our Detroit manufacturing hub and field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role and Your Impact

You own the way Aurelius is seen. The visual system, the narrative, the shots, the cuts, the stories we tell about what we’re building and the people building it. Factory floor in Detroit. Field tests on the range. Founders working late in SF. Lasers hitting drones at full power. All of it, through your lens.

We want someone who looks at the hardest stuff happening at the company and figures out how to make it feel as real and as important as it actually is. You’re not just capturing content, you’re building the way the world comes to understand directed energy and the team doing it in America. That’s a big seat for the right person who wants that kind of ownership.

You’ll travel with the team. You’ll be in the room for things most creatives never get to see. You’ll ship fast, you’ll shoot more than we can post, and you’ll have real ownership on what makes it out the door.

What You’ll Own

- Visual and narrative system for Aurelius across YouTube, X, and launch content

- Shoot, edit, and ship end to end. Camera to final cut

- Factory and shop floor documentation in Detroit and SF

- Field test coverage on the 400-acre range. Lasers hitting drones. Real footage, not stock

- Founder and ghost writing short, punchy, high-cadence

- Long-form product and launch films that set the standard for how defense tech gets shown

- The branding and company look. You make the hard engineering actually look as cool as it is

What We’re Looking For

- Shipped real YouTube. Channel, series, or long-form product or factory films you owned end to end

- Portfolio that proves it. Reel plus links. No resumes

- Gone viral or broken through on X or YouTube with hardware, industrial, auto, aerospace, or defense-adjacent work

- Set the look for something and then gotten behind the camera and cut it yourself

- Talked shop with at least one founder shipping real product, not just decks

- Native English speaker

Where You Probably Come From: Hardware or industrial YouTube channels you ran yourself. Auto, aerospace, or defense creative shops where you did more than one job. Studios where you were the whole stack from brief to delivery. Founder-adjacent creative seats where the content shipped fast and performed.

We Want to Talk If: You’ve built an audience from scratch on hard-to-film subjects. You’ve made industrial look beautiful. You’ve shot in environments most creatives would never go. You want the ownership and the range of a founding seat.

Not a Fit If: You direct and don’t shoot. You need an agency wrapper around you to work. Your reel is all polish and no substance.

How You Operate

- Bias for action. You shoot before you storyboard

- Travel without complaint. Detroit, SF, range sites, demos

- Comfortable embedded with engineers for hours getting one shot right

- Native taste for what’s cool and what’s filler

- Self-directed. You find the shot and go get it

Why Join Aurelius

- Direct report to the CEO

- Visual and narrative DNA of the company starts with you

- Real subject matter. Lasers, drones, factories, field tests. Not slide decks

- Your work ships to real audiences, not internal decks

- Travel the country shooting

title: Tax Manager
description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially minded Tax Manager to lead and manage the Group's direct tax compliance, tax advisory, and tax governance activities across the AMEA region. The role will be responsible for ensuring compliance with corporate income tax, withholding tax, and other direct tax obligations across multiple jurisdictions, while providing strategic tax advice to business stakeholders and supporting corporate initiatives. The successful candidate will also drive tax process improvements, strengthen internal controls, manage relationships with external advisors and tax authorities, and work with a team responsible for regional tax operations.
This is a high-visibility role that requires strong technical tax expertise, stakeholder management skills, and the ability to operate effectively in a complex multinational environment. It also represents a unique opportunity to join a small in-house global team of experienced tax professionals.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:

• Lead and manage corporate income tax, withholding tax, and other direct tax compliance obligations across jurisdictions.

• Manage quarterly and annual tax provision processes, including tax accounting and financial statement disclosures under IFRS and local GAAP.

• Serve as the primary tax advisor to business and finance stakeholders on cross-border transactions, business initiatives, and commercial arrangements.

• Provide technical guidance on corporate tax, withholding tax and international tax, impacting operations across jurisdictions.

• Monitor changes in tax legislation and regulatory developments across region and assess their impact on the business.

• Lead and coordinate responses to tax audits, tax authority enquiries, assessments, and disputes across the region.

• Identify and mitigate tax risks while ensuring appropriate documentation and support for key tax positions.

• Manage relationships with external tax advisors, auditors, and tax authorities to ensure high-quality and cost-effective support.

• Lead, coach, and develop regional tax team members, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

• Partner with Finance, Legal, Treasury, HR, and business leaders to support strategic projects, restructurings, and operational initiatives.

• Drive process improvement, standardization, and automation of tax compliance and reporting activities across AMEA.

• Support tax planning, cash repatriation strategies, and other initiatives aimed at optimizing the Group's overall tax position while maintaining compliance.

About You

• Professional accounting and/or tax qualifications as well as significant tax experience gained with a leading accountancy firm and/or an in-house multinational tax team.

• Previous related tax and accounting experience (10 to 15 years) with exposure to countries in the AMEA region will be of an added advantage.

• Highly motivated individual with appetite for working in a fast-paced and commercially oriented business.

• Organised and methodical individual, with the ability to plan and organise work effectively, delivering to deadlines.

• Excellent communicator, both verbally and written, adopting the most appropriate medium for the situation.

• Analytical, innovative, with good research and problem-solving skills.

• Experience of multiple-country CIT regimes and international tax aspects.

NVIDIA is looking for Senior Cloud Infrastructure/DevOps Solutions Architect to join its NVIDIA Infrastructure Specialist Team. Join the team building many of the largest and fastest AI/HPC systems in the world! We are looking for someone with the ability to work on a dynamic customer focused team that requires excellent interpersonal skills. This role will be interacting with customers, partners and internal teams, to analyze, define and implement large scale Networking projects. The scope of these efforts includes a combination of Networking, System Design and Automation and being the face to the customer!
What you'll be doing:

• Maintain large scale HPC/AI clusters with monitoring, logging and alerting Manage Linux job/workload schedulers and orchestration tools.

• Develop and maintain continuous integration and delivery pipelines

• Develop tooling to automate deployment and management of large-scale infrastructure environments, to automate operational monitoring and alerting, and to enable self-service consumption of resources.

• Deploy monitoring solutions for the servers, network and storage.

• Perform troubleshooting bottom up from bare metal, operating system, software stack and application level.

• Experience in managing and installing HPC clusters, including deployment, optimization, and troubleshooting.

• Experience with job scheduling workloads and orchestration technologies such as Slurm, Kubernetes, and Singularity.

• Proficiency in Python programming and bash scripting.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines for software deployment and automation.

• Comfortable with automation and configuration management tools, including Jenkins, Ansible, Puppet/Chef, etc.

• Ability to communicate technical concepts and collaborate effectively with Japanese-speaking customers.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Knowledge of CPU and/or GPU architecture .

• Knowledge of Kubernetes, container related microservice technologies.

• Experience with GPU-focused hardware/software (DGX, CUDA.)

• Background with RDMA (InfiniBand or RoCE) fabrics.

It also acts as the firm-wide clearing house for secondary transactions, including GP-led continuation vehicles and LP-led fund and co-investment buybacks. The team plays an active role in Investment Committee meetings and offers significant exposure to senior leadership across the firm.

title: Paid Search Strategist, DTC eCommerce
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
